Appendix.title: A star search and navigation contracts
Appendix.source: Concepts/A star search and navigation contracts.md
Appendix.Content: A* search and navigation contracts
A* is Dijkstra-style relaxation ordered by an estimate of the remaining cost. For node n,
Appendix.RawBlock: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"> <mi>f</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>n</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mi>g</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>n</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>+</mo> <mi>h</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>n</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>,</mo> </math>
Appendix.Content: where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>g</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>n</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> is the best path cost currently known from the start and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>h</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>n</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> estimates the cost from n to the goal.

The algorithm is not “put nodes in a priority queue and stop when the goal first appears.” Correctness depends on the edge-cost domain, heuristic assumptions, stale queue entries, and whether improved paths are allowed to reopen nodes.

With nonnegative edge costs and a zero heuristic, A* becomes Dijkstra’s algorithm. That is a useful oracle mode. An admissible heuristic never overestimates the true remaining cost; a consistent heuristic additionally satisfies a triangle-like condition and simplifies closed-set reasoning.
Relaxation
For edge n → m with cost c,

If this is smaller than the currently known <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>g</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>m</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>, update <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>g</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>m</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>, remember n as m’s parent, and push a new queue item. Priority queues commonly keep stale older entries; when popped, compare the queued score with the latest stored score and discard stale work.
A design that permanently closes a node before the heuristic assumptions justify that decision can return a suboptimal path.
Navigation is larger than A*

A navigation system also needs a graph construction story. For a navmesh this includes walkable geometry, polygon adjacency, portals, agent radius/height constraints, dynamic obstacle policy and a path-smoothing or funnel stage. A* only solves the discrete shortest-path problem on the graph it is given.
Executable reference
tools/labs/spatial_index_lab.cpp includes an A* implementation and tests a weighted graph using h = 0, making the expected result equivalent to Dijkstra’s optimum. It also checks an unreachable goal.
The witness does not yet prove navmesh generation, admissible geometric heuristics, funnel smoothing, dynamic replanning, hierarchical navigation or KairoSpatial parity.

Appendix.title: BVH build traversal and workload selection
Appendix.source: Concepts/BVH build traversal and workload selection.md
Appendix.Content: BVH build, traversal, and workload selection
A bounding-volume hierarchy is a tree whose nodes bound groups of primitives. Its purpose is not to make intersection magically faster; it is to let a query prove that large groups cannot matter.
For an overlap query Q, traversal follows a simple implication:
if Q does not overlap node.bounds, then Q cannot overlap any primitive below that node.

That pruning claim is only correct when every child primitive is actually contained by every ancestor bound. Tree construction therefore owns an invariant: each internal bound is the union of its children, and each leaf bound contains the primitives assigned to the leaf.
Build choices

A median split sorts or partitions primitive centroids and divides them into similarly sized groups. It is simple and usually avoids catastrophically unbalanced trees, but equal primitive counts do not imply equal traversal cost.
Surface-area heuristic construction estimates expected query/ray work. In the common ray-tracing interpretation, a split cost has the form

where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>A</mi> <mi>P</mi> </msub> </math> is parent surface area, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>A</mi> <mi>L</mi> </msub> <mo>,</mo> <msub> <mi>A</mi> <mi>R</mi> </msub> </math> are child areas, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>N</mi> <mi>L</mi> </msub> <mo>,</mo> <msub> <mi>N</mi> <mi>R</mi> </msub> </math> are primitive counts, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>C</mi> <mi>T</mi> </msub> </math> is traversal cost and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>C</mi> <mi>I</mi> </msub> </math> is primitive-intersection cost. Binned SAH approximates candidate split positions efficiently.

LBVH chooses hierarchy structure from Morton ordering. It can build quickly and map well to parallel hardware, but tree quality can be worse than a careful SAH build for some scenes. Which strategy wins depends on how often the scene rebuilds and how expensive later queries are.
Traversal representation
A production BVH must choose node layout as deliberately as split policy. Questions include:

ListItem.Content: binary versus wider nodes;
array indices versus pointers;
parent links or stackless encodings;
leaf primitive ranges;
AoS versus SoA bounds;
quantized bounds;
traversal stack depth and overflow behavior;
child ordering by query direction or distance.

Appendix.Content: For GPU traversal, divergence and memory coalescing can dominate the nominal tree complexity.
Dynamic scenes

Refitting recomputes ancestor bounds without changing topology. It is cheap when objects move modestly, but tree quality can decay. Rebuilding restores quality at higher cost. A useful dynamic policy measures a quality proxy and rebuilds when continued bad traversal is more expensive than reconstruction.
Dynamic AABB trees instead maintain a mutable hierarchy and often enlarge leaf bounds by a motion margin. The margin trades fewer reinserts for more false candidates.
Executable reference

tools/labs/spatial_index_lab.cpp builds a median-split BVH over deterministic random AABBs and compares 250 overlap queries against a brute-force oracle. Any missed or extra primitive is a test failure. The same laboratory also contains A* graph search with relaxation, reinsertion and unreachable-goal handling.
The witness does not claim SAH quality, LBVH construction, dynamic updates, SIMD traversal, ray packet behavior, navmesh construction, or KairoSpatial parity. Those remain separate evidence layers.
Related: AABB overlap and containment, Prefix scan and stream compaction, Field reordering and AoS versus SoA.
SAH, Morton and refit witness

tools/labs/bvh_sah_refit_lab.cpp advances the construction side beyond the earlier median-split query oracle. It computes prefix/suffix bounds for candidate partitions and minimizes the surface-area-weighted primitive cost, verifies that two separated three-object clusters split between the clusters, tests 3D Morton bit interleaving on a controlled monotone coordinate sweep, and refits a parent bound after one child moves.

This is enough to make the equations executable, but not enough to call the builder a production binned SAH or LBVH. A complete next layer needs fixed-bin accumulation, stable primitive partitioning, LBVH range/split construction from Morton prefixes, dynamic-tree rotations or reinsertion, and measured build-versus-query trade-offs on real workloads.

Appendix.Content: It maps angular velocity to angular momentum in body coordinates:
when the tensor and vector are expressed in compatible frames.
In world space, if body orientation is rotation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>R</mi> </math>,

Parallel-axis theorem
Moving the reference point away from the center of mass changes inertia:
Appendix.RawBlock: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"> <msub> <mi>I</mi> <mi>P</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>I</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mi>c</mi> <mi>m</mi> </mrow> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <mi>M</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="INNER"> <mo data-mjx-texclass="OPEN">(</mo> <mo data-mjx-texclass="ORD" fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo> <mi>d</mi> <msup> <mo data-mjx-texclass="ORD" fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo> <mn>2</mn> </msup> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mn mathvariant="bold">1</mn> </mrow> <mo>−</mo> <mi>d</mi> <msup> <mi>d</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mi mathvariant="sans-serif">T</mi> </mrow> </mrow> </msup> <mo data-mjx-texclass="CLOSE">)</mo> </mrow> <mo>,</mo> </math>

This is why using a collider-origin inertia as though it were a center-of-mass inertia couples translation and rotation incorrectly.
Scaling
Changing units does not change the physical body. Numerically converting metres to centimetres changes coordinate values and unit labels consistently.

Physically resizing a uniform-density object does change mass and inertia. Under uniform length scale <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>s</mi> </math> in 3D at fixed density, mass scales as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>s</mi> <mn>3</mn> </msup> </math> and inertia as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>s</mi> <mn>5</mn> </msup> </math>.

Appendix.title: DCC adapters and engine publication
Appendix.Content: DCC adapters and engine publication

A production pipeline should not let every DCC application define a different engine truth. Blender, Maya, Houdini and Nuke expose different object models, dependency systems and scripting APIs, but the engine-facing publication contract can remain host-neutral.
The useful separation is:

Content.Strong: Host adapter → normalized asset description → validation → deterministic build plan → staged publication → engine-side verification.

Appendix.Content: The host adapter owns how to read the authoring application. The normalized core owns what the engine requires. Publication owns filesystem and identity guarantees. Engine verification proves that the published result can actually be consumed.
Blender boundary

Blender’s Python API exposes application data through the bpy module, including data access, context, operators, types, utilities and path helpers. A production exporter should prefer direct data access for deterministic inspection and use context-sensitive operators only when their context requirements are understood.

An adapter should establish which evaluated scene state it exports, how collections and object visibility are interpreted, which transforms are baked, and which external dependencies are copied or referenced. Exporting the editable authoring graph and exporting evaluated geometry are different contracts.
Primary reference: https://docs.blender.org/api/main/index.html
Maya boundary

Maya exposes both scripting commands and C++/Python APIs, with explicit dependency-graph and DAG plug-in concepts. A Maya adapter should distinguish scene hierarchy from dependency relationships and should make attribute/default/reference semantics explicit rather than flattening everything into names.
Primary reference: https://help.autodesk.com/view/MAYADEV/2026/ENU/
Houdini boundary

Houdini’s Object Model exposes nodes and geometry through the hou package. SOP networks generate geometry, while ROP networks can describe render/output dependencies. Geometry references can also depend on node cook state, so an adapter must decide when data is evaluated and copied into the host-neutral representation.

SideFX documentation explicitly distinguishes node families such as SOP geometry, LOP/USD scene description, ROP output networks and TOP task workflows. A pipeline should use those semantics instead of treating every node graph as the same kind of data.
Primary references: - https://www.sidefx.com/docs/houdini/hom/ - https://www.sidefx.com/docs/houdini/
Nuke boundary

Nuke publication often involves image nodes, knobs, file paths and frame ranges rather than mesh topology. The engine-neutral contract should therefore represent sequence ranges and missing-frame policy explicitly. Frame range syntax can represent contiguous and stepped ranges, so “first and last frame exist” is not sufficient validation.
Primary reference: https://learn.foundry.com/nuke/content/getting_started/managing_scripts/defining_frame_ranges.html
Host-neutral core
A normalized publication record should carry at least:

ListItem.Content: logical asset identity;
schema version;
source provenance;
normalized relative input/output paths;
declared coordinate/unit/color-space conventions where relevant;
dependencies;
content identity or cryptographic digest;
frame range or subresource inventory;
tool/version information when reproducibility depends on it;
deterministic diagnostics.

Appendix.Content: The core should not contain live bpy, Maya, hou or Nuke objects. Those are host-lifetime objects. Convert them into owned normalized data before asynchronous work or engine publication.
Validation before mutation

A dry-run plan should be complete before writing outputs. Validate path traversal, duplicate output destinations, missing dependencies, unsupported schema versions, frame gaps and identity collisions first.

Then write to staging locations. Only after every staged artifact passes validation should publication become visible. On filesystems where atomic replacement is relied upon, that property needs an actual platform/filesystem test; a logical transaction model does not prove disk semantics.
Executable witness

tools/labs/production_pipeline_contract_lab.cpp implements the host-neutral part of this design. It validates a portable relative-path grammar, rejects parent traversal, checks schema and SHA-256 string shape, produces a deterministic sorted publication plan, checks output collisions, models idempotent publication, and verifies contiguous frame sequences.
It deliberately does not claim real Blender/Maya/Houdini/Nuke execution, SHA-256 computation, symlink resolution, atomic rename behavior or render-farm integration.
Related: Atomic publication and durability, Binary format contracts, Interface contracts and publication.
Executed Blender boundary

The host-neutral adapter contract now has one real DCC execution path. tools/dcc/blender_contract.py runs inside Blender in background mode, creates mesh/collection/object datablocks without UI interaction, attaches logical publication metadata, saves a .blend, exports a binary glTF/GLB with extras, validates the GLB header/JSON chunk, resets Blender, re-imports the GLB and verifies mesh identity plus custom publication fields.

The GitHub workflow .github/workflows/blender-dcc-contract.yml installs Blender on Linux and executes that round trip headlessly. This changes the Blender portion from “API described” to “host executed in CI.” It does not upgrade Maya, Houdini or Nuke: their adapters remain host-neutral contracts until a licensed/current host can execute them. It also does not prove arbitrary production scenes, armatures, materials, texture packaging or current Kairo import parity.

Current Blender documentation explicitly supports background Python execution and glTF export; the repository test treats those host APIs as an external boundary and validates the exported artifact rather than assuming an operator call succeeded.

Appendix.title: Impulse and force timing
Appendix.Content: Impulse and force timing
Force and impulse are related but they belong to different timing contracts.
Force is a rate of momentum change:
Impulse integrates force over time:
Appendix.RawBlock: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="block"> <mi>J</mi> <mo>=</mo> <msubsup> <mo data-mjx-texclass="OP">∫</mo> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <msub> <mi>t</mi> <mn>0</mn> </msub> </mrow> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <msub> <mi>t</mi> <mn>1</mn> </msub> </mrow> </msubsup> <mi>F</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mstyle scriptlevel="0"> <mspace width="0.167em" /> </mstyle> <mi>d</mi> <mi>t</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi> <mi>p</mi> <mo>.</mo> </math>
Appendix.Content: For constant mass and a linear impulse applied directly to the center of mass,

There is no additional timestep factor when applying an impulse that is already an integrated momentum change. Multiplying by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi> <mi>t</mi> </math> again turns the update into the wrong units.
For a force held constant through a numerical step,
so the timestep enters when converting the force into an approximate impulse.
Off-centre impulse

An impulse at world-space point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>p</mi> </math> relative to center of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>x</mi> </math> has lever arm
Angular impulse is
With world inverse inertia <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>I</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>−</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msup> </math>,
A contact solver uses this coupling when computing the effective mass seen along a contact direction.
Frame event versus physical force

A “jump button pressed” event should not necessarily apply the same force every rendered frame while the button remains down. A one-shot impulse, a force over a defined simulation interval, and a controller velocity target are different game/physics contracts.
The same issue appears with explosions, springs and contact responses.
Fixed step

Simulation forces should normally be accumulated and integrated on the fixed simulation clock. Rendering interpolation does not apply physics again. If multiple rendering frames occur between physics ticks, repeating a force per render frame introduces frame-rate dependence.
Verification

Test the same physical scenario with different render rates but the same fixed simulation step. For impulses, verify momentum change directly. For forces, integrate over equal physical time and compare trajectories/convergence order.
Read the connected explanation in Continuous Notes/Game Engine - From First Frame to Living Worlds#From the push on a panel to a repeatable rigid-body simulator.
Related: Center of mass and inertia, Time integrators and symplectic updates.
Constraint-level continuation

Forces change momentum over time; collision impulses change momentum at a discrete event. tools/labs/constraint_friction_island_lab.cpp now connects that distinction to a minimal sequential-impulse solver: an approaching normal velocity produces a nonnegative impulse that removes approach, a tangential impulse is clamped by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> <msub> <mi>j</mi> <mi>t</mi> </msub> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo stretchy="false">|</mo> </mrow> <mo>≤</mo> <mi>μ</mi> <msub> <mi>j</mi> <mi>n</mi> </msub> </math>, and repeated sweeps propagate support through a two-body stack.

The same witness builds contact islands with union-find. This makes a practical ownership boundary visible: contacts couple bodies inside an island, while disconnected islands may be solved independently. Angular effective mass, restitution thresholds, warm starting, sleeping and a full two-dimensional friction cone remain higher solver layers.

Appendix.title: Partial derivatives and gradients
Appendix.Content: Partial derivatives and gradients
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 9 · Latest development: Phase 9
Definition and mechanism

For a function of several inputs, a partial derivative varies one coordinate while holding the others fixed. Collecting these derivatives gives the gradient for a scalar-valued function. The gradient is a covector of first-order sensitivities: its pairing with a small displacement predicts the scalar change. Under the Euclidean inner product, the gradient vector points in the direction of steepest ascent, and its negative gives steepest local descent. Coordinate scaling changes derivative magnitudes and can therefore change optimization behavior. A partial derivative is not generally the full effect when inputs move together; that requires the total derivative or directional derivative. In graphics, gradients describe image sensitivity to geometry or material parameters, while their coordinates must be interpreted with the parameter units and basis used by the model.

Appendix.title: Production manifests and transactional publication
Appendix.Content: Production manifests and transactional publication

A production manifest is a durable description of what should be built and published. It prevents a pipeline from depending on hidden editor state or on “whatever files happen to be in this directory.”

A useful manifest separates identity from location. A logical asset ID names the thing the project means. Source and output paths say where a particular revision is read and written. A cryptographic digest can identify exact content bytes. A schema version says how to interpret all fields.
Path safety

Normalize paths before planning any write. A production-safe policy normally rejects parent traversal, unexpected absolute paths, ambiguous separators, and paths that escape the declared project root after symlink resolution.
Lexical normalization alone cannot prove symlink safety. The filesystem must be queried at the point where real paths are resolved, and the resolved target must still lie inside the approved root.
Deterministic plans
The same manifest and tool versions should produce the same ordered build plan. Determinism makes logs diffable, cache keys stable and failures reproducible.
Planning should be side-effect free. A dry run should reveal every intended output, overwrite, deletion and dependency before publication begins.
Staging and commit
A safe publication sequence is:

ListItem.Content: validate the whole request;
write derived outputs to staging names or directories;
validate staged bytes and metadata;
fsync or equivalent when durability is part of the promise;
publish with the platform’s proven atomic replacement mechanism;
update manifest/index state;
retain enough evidence to diagnose rollback or partial failure.

Appendix.Content: Atomicity and durability are separate. A rename can make a new name appear atomically yet still not guarantee survival across power loss unless the required data and directory metadata were persisted.
Idempotence

Repeating the same publication should either be a no-op or produce the same visible state. A pipeline that appends duplicate records, increments versions accidentally or rewrites unrelated timestamps on every run is harder to cache and reason about.
tools/labs/production_pipeline_contract_lab.cpp models deterministic plan generation and idempotent publication in memory. It intentionally labels real filesystem durability as unproved.
Related: Atomic publication and durability, DCC adapters and engine publication.

Appendix.title: Spring forces and numerical integration
Appendix.Content: Spring forces and numerical integration

For displacement from an endpoint to a particle, the ideal spring force preserves the sign of extension: stretching pulls toward the endpoint; compression pushes away. A bungee has zero force while slack and pulls only when stretched. Coincident endpoints need an explicit direction policy. Force magnitude alone cannot detect a direction error.

The force law and the time integrator are separate contracts. An undamped oscillator grows under forward Euler at every positive step size; semi-implicit Euler has a different bounded interval. An analytic target position does not become a reachable current-step position merely by converting it to force. Physical stiffness, mass-normalized coefficients and numerical damping settings need distinct units and definitions.

Appendix.title: Game Engine - Sources and Coverage
Appendix.Content: Game Engine — Sources and Coverage

This is the source ledger for Continuous Notes/Game Engine - From First Frame to Living Worlds. It is an audit companion, not another teaching volume. Captions, selected book passages, code snapshots, and original teaching remain different evidence types.
Coverage at 6 November 2026

The requested exhaustive video pass remains in progress. A retrieved caption file is not the same as a reviewed video. Full caption read means the cleaned caption text was read; it does not mean the on-screen code or final running project was visually inspected. Partial caption review records selected timestamp ranges and supports claims only within those ranges. Not reviewed must never be silently promoted because an episode title resembles a covered topic.

Kohi’s core playlist was enumerated at 395 positions. Travis’s channel inventory captured 573 unique metadata IDs across the inspected feeds; 426 were selected as engine candidates, including the TypeScript Engine series. Cherno’s six listed series total 234 positions; another 86 channel-video candidates expand its selected set to 320. Title-based discovery is an inclusion aid, not content analysis. Feed enumeration can omit private, removed, unlisted, or otherwise inaccessible material. These are captured scope counts, not a claim to know every unpublished source.

Kohi requests encountered HTTP 429, including after a later cooldown probe; unattempted videos remain explicitly unattempted. Some Cherno videos require sign-in/age verification and were not accessed. No authenticated-account or private Patreon content was accessed.

Appendix.Content: Executable and rendering verification

The original inline runtime_lab.cpp was compiled and run with Homebrew Clang 18.1.8 using -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror; it passed its timing-partition, interpolation, stale-handle, deferred-removal, capacity, overload, and invalid-duration assertions. The exact body also passed Apple Clang 21.0.0 with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer. An initial Homebrew sanitizer binary did not terminate during observation and was stopped; that run is not reported as passed.

The physics numeric witness checks the stated explicit/semi-implicit/constant-acceleration results and signed impulse/momentum example. These CPU tests are limited to the saved examples. They do not validate a windowed engine, graphics API integration, a complete collision solver, audio deadlines, network behavior, or editor interactions. Final local link, fence, Mermaid, MathJax, and code-body checks are recorded in the checkpoint reports.
Continuing this one volume

Keep future game-engine lessons in Continuous Notes/Game Engine - From First Frame to Living Worlds. Record their original source and supplied curriculum part numbers, define any prerequisite at first useful appearance, then weave the material into the relevant explanation. Retain missing/partial evidence states. The next source pass should prioritize unreviewed available captions, then retry only genuinely missing tracks when access permits. Do not redownload successful files or overwrite a final snapshot with an older module draft.
Batch 001 — capped acquisition and deeper reading

This continuation selected 50 already available caption sources for deeper review and a separate queue of at most 50 missing public captions for sequential acquisition. Eight new Kohi English captions were saved; the ninth request returned HTTP 429 and acquisition stopped immediately. The remaining 41 queue entries were not requested. Internal retries were disabled, with an eight-second gap between source requests. No authenticated or private content was accessed.

50 previously sampled sources were promoted to full-caption reads after complete cleaned-text reading. Sources not fully read retain their earlier partial status; merely putting a video into a 50-item queue does not count it as completed. The eight new captions remain not reviewed. Exact source IDs, transcript hashes, actual reading extent, acquisition logs, and before snapshots are in batches/batch-001/ under the research cache. The merged work/source-audit.json governs current counts over older channel-local snapshots.

Original pixel-layout and ray-picking numerical witnesses accompany the new teaching. The saved validation report states which final checks were executed. On-screen code, external engine builds, and native whole-book Obsidian layout remain unverified.
Batch 002 — full reading and audio transcription fallback

50 previously partial sources from the saved next50 queue received full cleaned-caption reads. 49 further YouTube caption tracks were retrieved across 49 sequential caption-source requests, with an eight-second pause and no internal retries. Including the single public-audio source request, acquisition remained capped at50 sources. See batches/batch-002/attempts.json for exact outcomes; a request cap does not imply every source succeeded.

The subtitle-free Kohi introduction dHPuU-DJoBM was processed from public audio using local OpenAI Whisper base.en (package20250625, CPU). The generated49-word VTT and raw model segments are retained separately from YouTube caption tracks. The entire generated text was read. The model misrecognized the project-name ending; that uncertainty is recorded and no technical claim is inferred from it. This is a full generated-text read, not manually verified transcription or visual inspection. Source audio/model/transcript hashes and exact generation configuration are preserved. Official Whisper reference.

Per-ID full-reading records, actual text extents, original before snapshots, generated-ASR provenance, and validation reports live in batches/batch-002/. Current counts come from merged work/source-audit.json, not older channel-local status files. The exhaustive source project remains unfinished; external engine builds, GPU/network/audio behavior, and whole-book native Obsidian layout remain untested.
Batch 003 — resumed reading, sequential acquisition, and audio ASR

50 incomplete saved-caption sources were promoted to full reads from the next50 queue, which originally contained29 sampled reviews and21 unread captions. One verified full-read record from an unfinished attempt was recovered rather than reread; its stored source text/hash and findings were retained. The remaining sources were read end-to-end in this continuation.

7 English YouTube caption tracks were saved across8 sequential caption-source requests, with an eight-second gap and internal retries disabled. Requests stop on the firstHTTP429. Public audio already cached for ImGui Events was reused for the audio fallback; no new request for that audio was made. The acquisition queue was capped at49 alongside that cached source. Exact source outcomes are in batches/batch-003/attempts.json.

Local OpenAI Whisper base.en, package20250625, CPU, generated 4286 words from the cached audio. The whole generated text was read. API names, code widths, and a repeated outro remain uncertain; the generated text is not a verbatim or manually audio-verified record. It is classified separately from YouTube captions. The reviewed text spans, audio/model/VTT hashes, contextual prompt, and ASR runtime parameters are preserved. The resulting teaching distinguishes historical narrated input plumbing from current primary guidance checked in the Dear ImGui FAQ and GLFW input guide.

All source-reading receipts, original snapshots, acquisition and transcription logs, teaching drafts, merge scripts, numeric witnesses, and actual validation reports are in batches/batch-003/. The merged work/source-audit.json governs current counts. Caption/ASR reading does not establish on-screen-code inspection, external-engine execution, or native whole-book Obsidian/PDF layout. The exhaustive project remains incomplete.
Batch 004 — render graphs, UI geometry, and renderer ownership

All 50 selected saved-caption sources were read end-to-end. The original queue contained 43 unread captions and seven sampled reviews. Ten unique full reads from the interrupted work were recovered using source hashes and normalized spoken-word counts; duplicate receipts were counted once. The final two sources were completed separately and reconciled against the exact original 50-source inventory.

Sequential acquisition saved 7 English YouTube tracks from 8 requests, eight seconds apart with internal retries disabled. Request eight returned HTTP 429 and acquisition stopped; 41 further queued caption sources were not requested. Public audio for Sparky: Ultra-Fast Batch Renderer was fetched once and reused during the continuation. Caption and audio requests together were capped at 50 sources. Exact outcomes remain in batches/batch-004/attempts.json and audio-acquisition.json.

Local OpenAI Whisper base.en, package 20250625, CPU, generated 17,680 words from that audio. The complete generated text was read. Technical names, integer-width wording and narrated performance claims remain uncertain; this is generated ASR, not a YouTube caption or manually audio-verified quotation. Audio/model/transcript hashes, model parameters, contextual hint, full reading receipt and uncertainty notes remain separate. No private or authentication-restricted source was substituted.

Teaching additions are organized around engine problems, including render-pass dependencies, resource staging, rotated UI hit tests, stencil clips, shader layouts, binary resources, audio lifecycle and indexed batches. The rendergraph ordering and UI inverse-transform examples have independent numerical witnesses. Historical implementation limits and unfinished fixes remain explicit.

Reading receipts, original snapshots, acquisition/transcription logs, synthesized additions and validation reports are retained in batches/batch-004/. The merged work/source-audit.json governs current counts. Reading captions or generated text does not establish inspection of video frames, source-code correctness, engine execution, or native whole-book Obsidian/PDF layout. The exhaustive all-video project remains unfinished.

The sample illustrates submit/flush, vertex-array/index-buffer binding, indexed drawing, and a queue-consumption bug. Preserve its per-object draw-call and per-frame matrix reconstruction limits; do not present the legacy API as current Hazel behavior.

Ep. 14: FreeImage — complements ### Make build and source organization part of maintenance and the renderer/API discussion under ## Give the renderer a clear job, then meet the graphics API. Map the external image library and its runtime dependency to build integration; map dimensions, bits per pixel, pitch, row direction, and channel interpretation to texture-data ingestion. Keep the exploratory debugging and legacy dependency explicit.

Visualizing Physics Colliders — maps to ### Keep the standard UI optional and stateful, but name its current limits for the settings toggle, ### Keep example behavior in the example application for editor/runtime separation, and ## Give the renderer a clear job, then meet the graphics API for overlay rendering. Preserve the concrete transform construction and the unresolved opposite-side circle visibility issue.

Ep. 4: Vectors — maps to the volume’s math and coordinate-space material, especially ### Camera and coordinate spaces and the graphics material under ## Give the renderer a clear job, then meet the graphics API. It supplies a historical vector value-semantics example; preserve the final fixes to non-mutating operators and avoid implying this source covers later direction math.

Ep. 24: Cleaning Up and Making a Game — maps to ### Make build and source organization part of maintenance, ### Keep example behavior in the example application, ### Keep engine lifecycle separate from game-specific frame work, and ### Packaging changes the host, not the engine’s obligations. Capture the feature freeze, extraction of game-specific tile behavior, application-loop sketch, texture batch limits, and portability intent; explicitly note that Emscripten completion is not shown.

Ep. 17: Texture Arrays — maps to #### From vertices to useful render operations and ### Keep renderer contracts small while the backend grows. The source actually uses a list of ordinary 2D texture bindings and per-vertex sampler slots, not a GPU texture-array object. Preserve the untextured color fallback, flush-on-capacity design, legacy slot count, and untested overflow path.

Ep. 10: Optimization and Maintenance — maps to ### Make build and source organization part of maintenance, #### API abstraction has a price, #### From vertices to useful render operations, and the existing matrix/allocator correctness material. Preserve the profiling method, relative-percent caveat, hard-coded-offset replacement, packed-color experiment, and temporary-buffer matrix fix; historical FPS numbers are not transferable benchmarks.

Ep. 12: Transformation Stack — maps to ### Camera and coordinate spaces and #### From vertices to useful render operations. It adds hierarchical object transforms and homogeneous position multiplication. Preserve transform composition order as version-specific, the identity-preserving pop guard, and the unresolved need for grouped submissions in the next episode.

Playing and Stopping Scenes (and Resetting) — maps to ### Keep example behavior in the example application, ## Keep identity, storage, and ownership in agreement, and the scene serialization/build material. The key contribution is copy-on-play scene isolation with UUID remapping and component transfer. Preserve the manually maintained component list and the reference-invalidation/debugging corrections as version-specific unfinished concerns.

Can AI Make a Game Engine? — maps to ## Know which story each source can tell and #### Source-to-volume map. It is evidence about a narrated prototype demonstration and its experiment setup, not inspected implementation quality. Keep the unequal run conditions, unresolved provenance, narrator’s pending code-review caveat, missing Forge controls, and bounded smoke-test claims explicit.

Community Issues/PRs and Merging Branches — maps to ## Know which story each source can tell, #### Source-to-volume map, and ### Make build and source organization part of maintenance. It documents branch integration, component-copy coverage, SDK/debug dependency changes, and scope-based contribution triage. Preserve that the keyboard-layout design remains unresolved and the renderer rewrite is future work in this episode.

Everything You Need in a 2D Game Engine (Hazel 2D) — maps to ### Put a rendering boundary between games and graphics APIs, ### Add scripting at a deliberate boundary, ### Integrate physics without surrendering the scene model, ### Build the editor around inspectable operations, ### Keep an audio front end separate from its playback backend, ## Prepare and publish content before promising it is ready, ### Generate platform projects from one configuration, then verify each target, ### Read performance results with the workload attached, and ### Packaging changes the host, not the engine’s obligations. This source is a Hazel 2D roadmap, not an implementation report: its explicit 2D focus, Hollow Knight-style target, and stretch goals are intentions. Preserve the roadmap as plans and do not convert them into completed implementation claims.

Reading/Writing C# Fields in Editor — maps to ### Scripts need a host, a lifecycle, and inspectable state, ### Treat editor panels as clients of live engine state, and ### Save scenes as a versioned authoring contract. Distinguish class-level field metadata from per-instance values, and mark edit-time persistence as deferred; only float controls are implemented in this episode.

Introduction to C++: Sparky Engine — maps to ### Make build and source organization part of maintenance, #### Precompiled headers as a measured project choice, ### Make build and source organization part of maintenance, and ## Keep identity, storage, and ownership in agreement. It is a historical language orientation for later Sparky episodes; preserve the platform-specific width caveat and the introductory limits around raw arrays and manual allocation.

C# Scripting! — maps to ### Scripts need a host, a lifecycle, and inspectable state, ### Add scripting at a deliberate boundary, and ### Managed scripts extend the host, not the engine's storage model. It adds a historical Mono embedding path: runtime/app-domain setup, managed assembly search paths, reflection for types, managed object construction, and native-to-managed method invocation. Preserve the Windows/Mono/Premake version context and the unresolved teardown race; entity integration, native internal calls, persistent authored values, and a complete editor workflow remain future work.

End-to-end disk event stepping and randomized supervision — November 12, 2026

An additional stand-alone C++20 laboratory at tools/labs/disk_event_pipeline_lab.cpp now connects continuous disk collision discovery to a complete fixed-duration state update. It repeatedly finds the earliest encounter among all unordered disk pairs, advances all positions to the event, groups approximately simultaneous events, freezes each incoming restitution target, runs 32 accumulated projected normal-impulse sweeps, and re-queries the remaining interval. Nine fixed scenes exercise collision timing against a static body, two-body elastic energy/momentum, symmetric simultaneous contacts, separating motion, initial overlap rejection, event budget failure, chained events, ideal inelastic response, and duplicate stable-ID / zero-duration validation.

Discovered defect and correction: the first nine scenes passed, but a separately constructed deterministic 10,000-case unequal-mass isolated-pair experiment failed at trial 937. A valid impact had advanced two centres to a near-tangent configuration whose squared distance was a tiny amount below the squared combined radius; the original squared-distance tolerance rejected it as a deep overlap. The published correction computes the linear centre gap and uses a finite-precision length tolerance scaled to world-coordinate magnitude. After this correction, all 10,000 seeded cases passed under GCC and Clang and sanitizer tests. No claim is made that this tolerance is globally robust for arbitrary very large/very small coordinate ratios.

The successful randomized experiment has been retained as independently executable tools/labs/disk_event_property_lab.cpp. For each isolated impact it checks exactly one event, Newton’s restitution equation, linear momentum conservation and non-increasing kinetic energy. Both newly published source files were re-fetched from GitHub and their Git blob hashes matched the locally compiled files: event pipeline e69b18ba580329db14ef0bde18811e6737790084 and property test caa2fffdfe32048e6580887ad868eda36278700f. Local strict C++20 GCC/Clang builds and combined AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer executions passed. The shared workflow is configured to run both on GitHub but its hosted execution has not yet been confirmed. The contact narrative and README now link both sources and explain the numeric trace.

Remaining boundary: this is not a production Kairo world step; all-pairs event search is quadratic per rescan, contact detection is constant-velocity disk-only, friction/rotation and resting contacts are excluded, and thrown exceptions can leave the scene partially advanced. Fully robust CCD predicates, broadphase acceleration, transactional state restoration, general convex shapes, long-time stacks, numerical determinism under compiler/platform changes and runtime integration remain open. No prior video/book claim-review queue counts were incremented by this engineering experiment.

The repository now contains tools/labs/swept_broadphase_lab.cpp, a tested reference implementation of constant-velocity disk swept-AABB candidate filtering. It conservatively constructs outward-rounded bounds, sorts by minimum x, tracks active x intervals and tests y overlap, then produces unique sorted candidate pairs. Each exact disk collision returned by a separately implemented analytic TOI oracle must be included in those candidates. The test covers a crossing scene, a 100-disk non-interacting scene, 200 seeded randomized 35-disk scenes, duplicate IDs and negative dt. The randomized comparison examines 200 × (35 × 34 / 2) = 119,000 possible pairs for missed collisions. GCC and Clang strict C++20 builds and a local combined AddressSanitizer/UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer build passed, and the GitHub source Git-blob SHA 11f9e86dbf1ee850e64b5dafdea63427b2177187 matched the compiled local source. The CI workflow includes this new lab but no GitHub-hosted run was confirmed here.

The broadphase is not integrated into the disk event stepper; it therefore establishes a conservative candidate-generation proof obligation in a small witness, not measured engine acceleration. Appendix.Content: Game Engine - Retrieval Card
Use this as a short teaching route, then follow the heading links for explanations, traces and code. The diagram shows responsibilities; it does not imply that every stage runs on a separate thread.

RowValue.Content: Initialization order follows dependencies; shutdown releases dependents first. A manager does not remove those edges.
[[Game Engine - From First Frame to Living Worlds#Keep engine lifecycle separate from game-specific frame work
Elapsed wall time and simulated time are separate. State catch-up, interpolation and pause policies before diagnosing movement.
[[Game Engine - From First Frame to Living Worlds#Make timestep and integration choices explicit
A storage index can move or be reused. Stable identity plus a generation/revision prevents stale references naming a replacement.
[[Game Engine - From First Frame to Living Worlds#A live object needs an identity that survives storage changes
Decode, validate and build a replacement before publication. CPU ownership and final GPU use are different lifetime facts.
[[Game Engine - From First Frame to Living Worlds#6. Asset publication connects files, runtime, and graph resources
Reads name versions; dependencies order users; compatible non-overlapping lifetimes may alias. Async schedules need actual completion edges.
[[Game Engine - From First Frame to Living Worlds#2. Compile a render graph before executing it

A splat index is not durable entity identity. Physical support supplies deformation; appearance alone supplies neither mass nor colliders.

New scene clears its path. Cancel is a no-op; failed writing keeps the dirty document. Save must choose authored versus runtime state explicitly.

The controller chooses input, zoom, speed and resize policy. A viewport change alone does not recompute projection.

Inputs need compatible state/simulation; snapshots need interpolation; captured video limits camera freedom. Edited retellings are separate from authoritative records.

Trace immediate reward and delayed consequences together. Shooting a segment can remove danger while creating mushrooms and split threats.

Authored context and emergent play histories cooperate. Make state changes legible before assuming players understand their consequences.

Record the rule, exception, intended experience and evidence status. A large specification is not proof that play works.
[[Game Engine - From First Frame to Living Worlds#A design document is a working reference, not a frozen game

An enclosing parent bound can overlap a candidate that misses both children: broad-phase inclusion is a possibility, not a collision. Reopen the scaled witness and its distances.
For the separate contracts of pixel footprint, compositing order and storage reuse, use Figure ER1 and its caption.

Before teaching a topic, reconstruct one failure trace: which invariant was violated, what visible symptom followed, and which measurement isolates the first wrong state? A successful build, a correct CPU formula and a correct native frame are different kinds of evidence.
Trace a confusing action: context → visible option → accepted action → changed state → visible result. Reopen the five-stage choice figure and door trace.
Stable IDs: random identifiers need a bit-width/count model and a collision policy. Figure E-ID compares the assumptions; a display name or temporary entity slot is a different kind of identifier.
Contact candidates, active constraints, and surviving identities
Read the figure: retaining a key preserves a candidate, not a force. Refresh its geometry before deciding whether it belongs in this step’s active constraints; validate any old impulse separately.

No: diagonal corner distance can exceed the radius. A 0.30-radius sphere at (1.25,1.25,0) misses a unit-half-extent box.

No. Its bounds depend on w; x=2,w=2 lies on the right plane.

Cell.Content: Compressed ordinary spring versus slack bungee?
Ordinary spring pushes apart; bungee has zero compression force. With k=8 N/m and rest length1m, half-length spring gives +4N outward.

Translation and small rotation shift shared points; project their relative shift onto the frozen normal and search severity again.

No: a 45 N push needs 45 N, below a 60 N limit. The coefficient describes the material pair.

Under the stated drag-free horizontal-launch model, gravity must fall four hundredfold.

Cell.Content: Does a successful thread-status query mean the job succeeded?

This companion appears in Volume 2, The Visual Computing Bible — Volume II: Computational Geometry, Vision, Reconstruction and XR: Bounding volume hierarchies — Bounding volume hierarchies Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: University courses · Latest development: University courses Definition and mechanism A bounding volume hierarchy (BVH) organizes primitives into a tree of enclosing boxes. An internal node’s box contains the boxes of its children; a leaf stores a small set of triangles. To trace a ray, test the root box, recurse only into intersected children, and compare triangle hits in reached leaves. A box miss safely rejects every primitive beneath it, so the hierarchy reduces expensive exact tests when geometry is spatially coherent. Construction chooses how to group primitives and where to split; a surface-area heuristic estimates expected traversal work, while simpler median splits are faster to build. Dynamic scenes may refit boxes after deformation or rebuild the hierarchy when overlap grows. Correctness requires every primitive to remain enclosed; performance depends on tree quality and ray distribution. Prerequisites
Ray-triangle intersection Manifold polygon meshes and boundary structure
Used by
Worlds, Images and Inference Radiance fields and Gaussian splatting ## Full teaching explanation
Acceleration structures and robust queries · Visibility queries and ray intersections. Open Bounding volume hierarchies in Volume 2

Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 2, The Visual Computing Bible — Volume II: Computational Geometry, Vision, Reconstruction and XR: ODE integration and stability — ODE integration and stability Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: University courses · Latest development: Phase 9 Definition and mechanism An ordinary differential equation gives the rate of change of a state over time. Forward Euler uses the current derivative: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>q</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mi>k</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <msub> <mi>q</mi> <mi>k</mi> </msub> <mo>+</mo> <mi>h</mi> <mi>f</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msub> <mi>q</mi> <mi>k</mi> </msub> <mo>,</mo> <msub> <mi>t</mi> <mi>k</mi> </msub> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>h</mi> </math> is the time step. For decay <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mover> <mi>u</mi> <mo>˙</mo> </mover> </mrow> <mo>=</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mi>a</mi> <mi>u</mi> </math>, it multiplies each step by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>1</mn> <mo>−</mo> <mi>a</mi> <mi>h</mi> </math>; if the magnitude exceeds one, the numerical solution grows even though the true solution decays. Spring systems can be stiff because high-frequency modes force very small stable steps. Backward Euler evaluates the rate at the unknown new state and is more stable for decay but requires solving an equation and may add numerical damping. Symplectic Euler updates velocity then position and often keeps energy bounded for conservative mechanics. Choose an integrator according to stability, accuracy, conservation, and runtime rather than displayed frame rate alone. Phase 9–10 development An initial-value problem consists of a differential equation and a specified starting state. A numerical integrator replaces continuous evolution with finite updates, so accuracy and stability depend on both method and step size. Consistency concerns local approximation, stability concerns error growth under repeated steps, and convergence concerns the limiting solution as the step is refined. Stiff systems can force explicit methods to take very small steps even when the visible trajectory changes slowly. Symplectic methods preserve Hamiltonian structure but do not generally preserve exact energy at each step. Prerequisites
Absolute and relative error Conditioning and singularity ODE initial-value problems and stiffness Time integrators and symplectic updates
Used by
Worlds, Images and Inference Implicit differentiation and parameter sensitivities
Full teaching explanation Dynamics, forces, and numerical integration · Animation curves and motion paths - Phase 9 teaching section - Visual Recall/09 - Calculus and Optimization - Visual Recall.md · Phase 9 visual recall. Open ODE integration and stability in Volume 2

Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 2, The Visual Computing Bible — Volume II: Computational Geometry, Vision, Reconstruction and XR: Camera view and clip-space pipeline — Camera view and clip-space pipeline Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase7 · Latest development: University courses Definition and mechanism A camera pose maps camera coordinates to world coordinates; its inverse is the view map. Projection produces homogeneous clip coordinates, clipping applies the API-specific inequalities, and valid perspective division produces NDC. Storage order supplies none of these coordinate contracts. Reconstruction cue: A standard minus-Z perspective example needs a point in front of the camera and a meaningful clip w before division. Prerequisites
Coordinate frames and change of basis
Used by
Phase 7 teaching and laboratory Depth buffering and visibility order Lens optics and depth of field GPU vertex specification Homogeneous clipping and perspective interpolation Axial depth and Euclidean range Hardware depth-buffer linearization Screen-space ray generation and mouse picking Ray differentials and camera sampling measures
Recall and next depth Reconstruct the example, state its conventions and find an input that violates its preconditions. Deeper algorithms and measured production performance remain separate from the present model. Source and navigation Continuous explanation · Coverage and source gap · Sources and verification University course development Extend the existing transform pipeline with the clipping and depth-precision decisions that make projection robust. A view frustum is the set of points a camera can see, bounded by near and far planes as well as image sides. Transforming the frustum into a canonical clip cube makes outside tests cheap; partially intersecting triangles must be clipped and triangulated so the rasterizer still receives triangles. The near plane also avoids geometry crossing the eye plane, while the far plane limits depth range. Floating-point depth values are unevenly distributed after perspective division, so an excessively tiny near distance paired with a huge far distance can make two nearby surfaces quantize to the same depth and produce z-fighting. Choose the narrowest useful depth interval and keep the view, clip, normalized, and screen coordinates distinct. A scene description becomes an image · Cameras, projection, and calibration · Rasterization, coverage, and depth Phase 11 camera development A raster-to-ray camera maps a pixel to a geometric sample; In a pinhole model, invert projection and view transforms to recover a camera-space direction, then transform it to world space without applying translation as if it were a point. Pixel-center convention, viewport origin, handedness, clip-depth range, and normalization all affect the result. Offset a pixel to generate differential rays and estimate the surface footprint; that footprint grows with depth and changes with surface orientation. Keep ray generation distinct from raster projection while ensuring their conventions agree. Link: A camera model must close the loop; research: Four deeper links from the TUM lecture review.. Open Camera view and clip-space pipeline in Volume 2

Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 1, The Foundations Bible — Volume I: From Bits to Computation, C++, Memory and Systems: Corpus Development Audit - 2026-11-12 — Three-volume corpus development audit — 12 November 2026 Scope and verified repository state Baseline for the first consolidation: 89c386f25b361685051bb035799014c8875487cd. The consolidation was merged as 635dec49e67fc31f377b8f9f638a458a0b5a9abb. The subsequently inspected main head was e25a8095815944a19e3ea3a3f69c40b7c90dd6fb. This audit uses the contents of that later main head rather than assuming the merge remained the latest state. The new render-graph source-to-volume exercise in this continuation is additive to that baseline; distinguish its branch tests from merged main checks. The three canonical continuous books are Mathematics, Graphics, and Game Engine. The repository still retains four archival source copies under Continuous Notes/ (Computing Foundations, XR, Rigid Bodies, Systems), making seven physical Markdown files in that folder. They are retained as reversible provenance, not designated further required books; this is an organizational compromise to be resolved only after a backlink and preserved-source audit. The source-preservation checker verifies exact migrated body inclusion or original-line-preserving additive expansions, alongside canonical original line-order preservation; it is intentionally not proof that all original content is coherently taught at first use. Change-by-change assessment Change Current evidence Remaining decision / failure mode Mathematics canonical volume Affine-frame inverse / reciprocal-basis C++20 witness inline and independently in tools/labs/basis_measurement_lab.cpp. Exact-code inclusion and release-safe checks passed GitHub regression. Numeric example is a 2D host representation, not a general 3D inverse, GPU shader ABI, ill-conditioning proof or all-input overflow-safe solver. Add property-based tests and explain transformations when first used. Graphics canonical volume Full former XR source and shader-buffer/GPU execution teaching migrated. Existing geometry, CCD and raster code retained. A long XR insertion appears before much of the main coordinate-frame teaching; unedited source chapter headers and old backlinks can disrupt continuity. GPU performance and shading rules need driver captures/reference comparisons. Game Engine canonical volume Full formerly separate bits/C++/CPU/algorithms, explicit backend, rigid-body and emulator/system bodies migrated. Spring, contact refresh and game-system framing added after merge with source-synced C++ witnesses. The huge foundation insertion comes before the normal engine startup narrative. Source presence is not the same as teaching at the implementation’s first meaningful use. Important GPU backend and production Kairo claims remain unverified. Tests and source agreement Three-volume exact-substring/ordered-line audit and continuous embedded-code agreement succeeded. New render_graph_contract_lab.cpp expands a conceptual graph into runnable RAW/WAR/WAW/topological and negative tests. Full volume semantic review, all snippets building on every supported compiler, GPU barriers, all source units and production-engine integration have not been proven. Review/source ledger Latest inspected checkpoint records 26,821 reviewed claim-text points and 2,894 pending, out of 29,715 registered point claims over 590 retained records. “Reviewed” is a saved claim-text reading receipt, not complete raw-video truth verification, complete textbook reading, or source integration. Never revert to the older 14,240/15,475 snapshot when reporting current state. The repository’s latest main CI at inspection passed the C++20 regression, continuous-source agreement and three-volume preservation workflows. The previous release-only assert defect was repaired by using explicit runtime checks, so -DNDEBUG no longer disables the basis laboratory’s validation. Navigation and first-use risks found by the live link inventory The three books contained approximately 23 links into the old archival volumes at the inspected head: 1 from Mathematics, 11 from Graphics and 11 from Game Engine. The source targets still exist, so these are mostly legacy detours, not missing files. Nevertheless they violate the spirit of one reader-facing continuous destination per subject. Their replacement requires determining which in-book heading now owns each prerequisite; a blanket text substitution would break provenance and risk moving a reader to the wrong derivation. Until reconciled, the old link is supporting provenance rather than an instruction to start a fourth book. A first-pass wiki-link regex reported spurious missing targets such as nodiscard, no_unique_address, GPU attributes and media paths. Those are often C++/shader syntax, escaped expressions, or images, not Obsidian page links. An audit tool must ignore fenced/inline source and distinguish image attachments from Markdown notes before treating these as missing content. Heading existence itself also proves only the presence of a title, not a coherent implementation. The Engine source insertion is particularly large and now occupies roughly forty thousand lines before the original mid-engine renderer material. Graphics also contains an early full XR source block. These are high-priority reading-flow issues even though the mechanical content-preservation checks are green. Preserve original words, but use linking, carefully justified section placement and substantive bridge explanations to make the story follow a recurring engine problem rather than a pasted source queue. Implementation-depth contract for every developed concept A reader should be able to close the book and build the mechanism. Therefore a concept is not “done” until its first meaningful use provides: the forcing engineering problem; definitions of every symbol, convention and unit; the derivation and its assumptions; the concrete memory/state representation and ownership; the full algorithm and decision branches; a complete documented implementation or a clearly labeled API-specific implementation; a numerical trace with inspectable intermediate state; failure/degeneracy and alternatives; proof of invariants and bounded behavior; and reproducible positive, negative and metamorphic tests. The note itself must contain these, not just a heading, a pointer to a video, or a code file that the reader must discover elsewhere. Witness categories must remain distinct. A CPU-only pedagogical model can prove logic, arithmetic and expected rejection cases. It cannot prove production GPU memory visibility or Apple/NVIDIA driver behavior. A reference engine test cannot establish the current Kairo integration unless the exact Kairo commit and reproducible build are inspected. A mathematically derived assumption is not an observed result; a video transcript’s claim is not verified code; the 3,000-part route map is an ownership assignment rather than 3,000 completed reconstructions. Current development increment: logical render-graph compiler The Game Engine volume now carries a full C++20 pass-graph compiler inline at the point where renderer intent becomes backend work. The independent laboratory is tools/labs/render_graph_contract_lab.cpp, source-synchronized through tools/check_continuous_code_sync.py. It builds a DAG from per-resource last-writer and reader-cohort state, records RAW/WAR/WAW hazards, handles imported history, topologically sorts with deterministic tie-breaking, and rejects duplicate resources, uninitialized transient reads, feedback and explicit cycles. The six-pass G-buffer/shadow/lighting/temporal/tone-map/present trace and negative cases make those semantics inspectable. GCC and Clang compiled/reran the reference locally with -O1 and -O2 -DNDEBUG, warnings-as-errors. Boundary: This is a single-queue logical whole-resource compiler, not an implemented Vulkan or Metal render graph. It does not emit stage/access masks, image layout transitions, queue-family ownership, timeline waits, transient aliasing or device-loss recovery. Those remain first-class milestones, not implicit features of this passing laboratory. See the Vulkan synchronization specification for the separate memory-model obligations. Next priority queue with acceptance criteria
Remove legacy reading detours without losing evidence. Resolve each old note backlink to the exact newly embedded canonical heading and explain domain-specific prerequisites locally; keep exact raw source copies under version control. Audit inline C++ attributes and image paths separately, avoiding false link positives. Review the remaining 2,894 source claim-text points against their actual units, update review receipts, and directly enrich Mathematics/Graphics/Game Engine where an inspected claim reveals an underdeveloped first-use explanation. Do not infer transcript/audio validity from the claim text. The saved local backlog identified by the source ledger may be unavailable from remote GitHub; do not fabricate receipts. Develop GPU transitions from the logical render DAG with explicit Vulkan synchronization2 and Metal-specific resource rules, CPU reference graphs, recorded device-validation output and cross-backend parity. Expand to per-mip/layer/aspect and history versioning before claiming transient reuse. Prove implementation readiness instead of matching headings. For every mapped original part, record the exact in-book implementation destination, executable/source identity, derivation, worked trace, failures and production evidence if claimed. Preserve missing or unreceived parts and distinguish reconstructed teaching from source-provided lessons. Complete outstanding books/captions and repository-grounded case studies in bounded audited batches. Never convert older source book/course titles into a claim that every page, second of video, or current project branch has been inspected.
This report is an audit checkpoint and development instruction embedded in the repository, not a certificate that the entire curriculum is complete.. Open Corpus Development Audit - 2026-11-12 in Volume 1

It induces distance by taking the norm of a point difference. Coordinate-defined first, second and infinity norms answer different geometric questions. For <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>3</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mn>4</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>, the three norms are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>7</mn> </math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>5</mn> </math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>4</mn> </math>. Squared length scales quadratically and is not itself a norm or induced metric. Prerequisites

This companion appears in Volume 1, The Engine Builder's Bible — Volume I: From First Frame to Core Runtime Systems: Field reordering and AoS versus SoA — Field reordering and AoS versus SoA Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: C003 · Latest development: C003 Definition and mechanism Reordering fields can reduce alignment holes: conventional 1/8/1/4 members shrink 24→16 bytes when arranged 8/4/1/1. AoS (array of structures) interleaves full records; SoA (structure of arrays) separates each field into its own array. Smaller records do not prove faster code; hot fields and access patterns matter, and layout changes may break ABI. Prerequisites

Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 2, The Foundations Bible — Volume II: Numerical Methods, Probability, Geometry and Camera Systems: Derivative as a local linear map — Derivative as a local linear map Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 9 · Latest development: Phase 9 Definition and mechanism The derivative measures first-order change. In one variable it is the limit of the difference quotient; in several variables it is the linear map that best predicts small output changes near a point. For a scalar function, this local model is the tangent line. For a vector-valued function, it is a matrix acting on an input perturbation. The derivative is local: its approximation error becomes small relative to the perturbation as the step shrinks, but the linear model need not remain accurate over a large region. This view unifies instantaneous velocity, gradients, Jacobians, and optimization directions. It also gives a practical check: compare a small finite perturbation with the derivative’s predicted change, while remembering that floating-point rounding and curvature limit how small or large the perturbation should be. Prerequisites
No earlier concept node is required in this planned path.
Used by

In orthonormal real coordinates the dot is a sum of component products. Its geometric form is length product times angle cosine. Orthogonality means zero inner product; zero itself has no angle. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>3</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>4</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>⋅</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mn>6</mn> </math>, while the cosine is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>6</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>5</mn> <mo>⋅</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0.6</mn> </math>. Coordinate dotting assumes the correct metric. Prerequisites

Appendix.title: Cross-volume companion reference
Appendix.Content:
This companion appears in Volume 2, The Foundations Bible — Volume II: Numerical Methods, Probability, Geometry and Camera Systems: Time integrators and symplectic updates — Time integrators and symplectic updates Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 9 · Latest development: Phase 9 Definition and mechanism A time integrator turns a differential equation into a discrete state update. Explicit Euler uses the current slope; midpoint and Runge–Kutta methods combine several slope evaluations to improve local accuracy; semi-implicit Euler updates velocity before position and can behave better for mechanical systems. Symplectic methods preserve the geometric structure of Hamiltonian dynamics, often keeping long-run energy error bounded rather than allowing systematic drift. No method is universally best: order, stability region, cost, conservation, and stiffness all matter. A higher formal order does not guarantee better behavior at an unsuitable step size or under discontinuous forces. Compare integrators on the same problem, step policy, and error target. Update order is part of the algorithm: changing it can change stability and physical behavior, not merely code style. Prerequisites
ODE initial-value problems and stiffness
Used by
ODE integration and stability
Full teaching explanation

This companion appears in Volume 2, The Foundations Bible — Volume II: Numerical Methods, Probability, Geometry and Camera Systems: Function contracts: domains, codomains, and images — Function contracts: domains, codomains, and images Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 9 · Latest development: Phase 9 Definition and mechanism A function is a rule that assigns exactly one output to every allowed input. Its domain states which inputs are valid; its codomain states the declared output set; its image is the subset actually reached. These sets affect whether an inverse exists and whether a formula is defined at a boundary. For example, squaring maps the real line into nonnegative outputs but is not one-to-one until its domain is restricted to nonnegative values. In a camera map, division by depth makes zero depth invalid, while a positive-forward convention further restricts visible points. Treating these as contracts makes composition safer: the output of one function must lie in the next function’s domain. A typed implementation can encode some, but not all, of these mathematical restrictions. Prerequisites
No earlier concept node is required in this planned path.
Used by

F09-2. Accumulated area and the derivative that recovers the integrand. For A(x)=x cubed/3 at x=1.8, A=1.944 and A prime=3.24=x squared.
F09-3. Quadrature error as sample intervals increase. For exp(x) on [0,1] at N=16, left-rule error is about 0.053137, trapezoid error 5.593e-4, and Simpson error 1.456e-7; Simpson uses an even interval count.
F09-4. Energy behavior for the stated harmonic-oscillator step size. At h=0.1 for 80 periods, explicit Euler energy reaches about 2.62e21, semi-implicit Euler stays in [0.47619,0.526316], and RK4 ends near 0.499965. This is the plotted setup, not a universal ranking.
F09-5. Full Newton step versus Armijo backtracking for the plotted log-cosh example. At x=3, the full step is about -100.8566; backtracking first accepts alpha=0.03125 in this setup.
F09-6. Central-difference truncation and roundoff for sin(x) at x=0.7. The analytic derivative is cos(0.7), about 0.7648422; the best sampled step has error about 8.94e-13.
